user_prompt: How should we notify customers about 20 minutes of downtime tomorrow night?
positive_response: Please be advised that scheduled infrastructure maintenance will take place tomorrow at 22:00 UTC. The platform will be temporarily inaccessible for approximately twenty minutes. We appreciate your patience.
contrast_response: Hey everyone! Quick heads up that we're doing some maintenance tomorrow night around 10 PM UTC. Things will be down for about 20 mins while we update things. Thanks for hanging tight!

scenario: Explain sprint delay to team lead
user_prompt: How do I tell my lead the auth task is running 1 day late?
positive_response: I am writing to provide an update regarding the authentication module. Due to unforeseen edge cases in session revocation, completion will be delayed by one business day. I anticipate delivery by Wednesday afternoon.
contrast_response: Hey, just wanted to give you a quick ping on the auth task. Ran into a couple tricky edge cases with session handling, so looks like I'll need another day on this. Should have it wrapped up by Wednesday afternoon!
invariant_summary: Both communicate a 1-day delay on the auth module due to edge cases, with completion on Wednesday.

scenario: Draft a message to a client explaining a scheduled maintenance downtime
user_prompt: How should I professionally inform my client about the downtime next week?
positive_response: We wish to inform you that our services will be temporarily unavailable for scheduled maintenance on Thursday at 8 AM. Please ensure that all critical tasks are completed by Wednesday noon to accommodate this necessary interruption.
contrast_response: Hey there! Just wanted to give you a heads up that we're going to be down for a bit next week. Maintenance's gotta be done on Thursday at 8 AM, so you might wanna wrap up any urgent stuff before that.
invariant_summary: Both the high-formality and low-formality responses inform the client about the downtime occurring on Thursday at 8 AM and advise completing critical tasks before this period. The only difference lies in the tone and language style used, with the formal response using a professional register and tone, and the informal response adopting a casual and friendly tone.

scenario: Respond to a coworker asking how to set up their local dev environment
user_prompt: Could you guide me on setting up my local development environment?
positive_response: Certainly. To configure your local development environment, you must first install the necessary software packages. You may start by acquiring a virtual machine like VirtualBox or VMware, or alternatively, set up a containerized environment using Docker. Proceed by installing an Integrated Development Environment (IDE) such as Eclipse or Visual Studio Code, followed by selecting a programming language, for instance, Python, and then establishing a version control system like Git. Lastly, clone your project's repository and install any required libraries or frameworks, as delineated in the project's documentation.
contrast_response: Sure thing! To get your local dev setup going, grab a tool like VirtualBox or VMware, or you could go for Docker. Then pick an IDE that suits you, like Eclipse or VSCode, and pick a language, say Python. Oh, and make sure to set up Git for version control. Once you clone the project from the repo, just follow the docs for any extra tools or libraries that need to be installed.
invariant_summary: Both the high formality and low formality responses provide a step-by-step guide on setting up a local development environment. They include instructions on installing virtualization software, selecting an IDE, setting up version control, cloning a project, and installing any additional tools or libraries, as per the project documentation.

scenario: Welcome a new contributor to an open-source project repository
user_prompt: How should I formally welcome a new contributor to our repository?
positive_response: We are delighted to introduce you to the team. Your participation in our project is highly valued, and we eagerly anticipate the unique perspectives and contributions you will bring to our collaborative endeavor.
contrast_response: Hey there! Welcome aboard. We're super pumped to have you on the team. Your ideas are gonna shake things up for the better, so let's get cracking and build something amazing together.
invariant_summary: Both responses invite the newcomer to join the project and express enthusiasm for their involvement. The invariant factual claims/answers, in this case, are the acknowledgement of the new contributor's value and the anticipation of their contributions. The formality level, in terms of language and tone, is the distinguishing factor between the two responses.
